title: HTML is All You Need (for Agents to Make Graphics) - Amol Kapoor, Nori
talk_summary: Amol Kapoor argues agents fail at graphics not because of spatial reasoning limits but because SVG/canvas tools are the wrong medium; HTML/CSS, which models have seen billions of examples of, lets them express layout as structure and the browser renders pixels. He shows this used for slide decks, docs, and video, and recommends giving agents direct data access to build artifacts end-to-end.

takeaways.what_they_do: Instead of having agents manipulate canvases, SVGs, or PowerPoint CLIs, they have agents emit HTML/CSS and let the browser render to pixels/PDF, so the model reasons in tags and structure rather than coordinates.
takeaways.evidence_quote: HTML lets the model think in structure. HTML tags have meanings built into the language.

takeaways.technique: Design tools around model priors, not human workflows
takeaways.what_they_do: They argue agent tools should match the model's native medium (tokens/structure) rather than mimicking human GUI workflows like click-drag or screenshot-and-replace loops.
takeaways.evidence_quote: You need to give the AI tools based on how it thinks, not in pixels, in language.

takeaways.technique: Pick the arbitrary intermediate format agents are best at
takeaways.what_they_do: They note the editing format is arbitrary as long as the final render is correct, so they choose HTML as the intermediate representation and convert to PDF only at the end.

takeaways.technique: Give agents direct data access to build artifacts end-to-end
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than hand-assembling content, they give the model access to company data (call transcripts, emails) so it populates the artifact itself.
takeaways.evidence_quote: If you just give the model access to your data, say your call transcripts or your emails, you can have the model build the deck end to end.
